schema.body:
# Fixture schema

A synthetic vault for reconciliation execution tests. Arc states: open, closed, abandoned. Inquiry states: open, ready_for_synthesis, resolved. Problem states: draft, accepted, obsolete. Design states: draft, proposed, accepted, superseded. Preserve IDs, types, and graph edges. Repository validation is supplied by the harness. No force_accept or override_blocking exists.

cache-arc.body:
# Cache arc

All inquiries are resolved, but the objective changed. The owner has not chosen between closing the completed work and abandoning the obsolete objective. Both remain plausible.

latency-arc.body:
# Latency arc

The owner records that this arc met its completion conditions: every inquiry is resolved and the measured latency target was reached. No work remains; close the arc.

rollout-arc.body:
# Rollout arc

Closure has been requested, but rollout-inquiry remains open.

legacy-design.body:
# Legacy design

This design is still accepted and frames old-problem. No superseding design is recorded.

old-problem.body:
# Old problem

The owner says this problem no longer describes current needs and proposes obsolete. An accepted design still frames it.

paused-design.body:
# Paused design

Work is paused pending the cache objective decision; no final status is authorized.

paused-problem.body:
# Paused problem

The cache objective needs an owner decision.

secondary-problem.body:
# Secondary problem

This remains relevant. It is connected to latency-arc, not directly to latency-inquiry.

unpaired-problem.body:
# Unpaired problem

Users need a better rollout explanation. No design or shelving choice has been made.

rollout-choice.body:
# Rollout choice

Prefer rollout if rollout-inquiry clears its dependency. Compare it with the cache decision and a design for unpaired-problem. A relationship between rollout-arc and unpaired-problem may explain shared users; verify the graph before recommending a new edge.

2026-10-20-reconciler-dream.body:
# Reconciler dream — 2026-10-20

Window: last 30 days. Generated by the reconcile-vault dream pass.

## Needs you

- latency-arc: resolve the repository validation failure before closure; legacy export rejects closed latency-arc. The attempted closure was reverted.
- rollout-arc: resolve rollout-inquiry before reconsidering closure; blocked by arc_all_inquiries_closed.
- cache-arc: choose closed or abandoned; the changed objective leaves both plausible (cache-options).
- old-problem: review the accepted legacy-design relationship before obsoleting; warning problem_brief_obsolete_warns_framers.
- ready-inquiry: write and assess the missing synthesis before resolving; completion evidence is absent.
- paused-design: decide whether the pause remains appropriate after choosing the cache objective; no final status is supported.
- unpaired-problem and secondary-problem: commission designs or explicitly document shelving reasons; accepted status alone does not explain the missing designs.

## Part A — Graph hygiene

### Activity heatmap

| Scope | Total | Recent | Last activity |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| performance | 9 | 6 | 2026-10-20 |
| legacy | 8 | 2 | 2026-10-19 |

Performance dominates recent activity, with six recent artifacts versus two in legacy. Neither scope has zero recent activity; no retirement candidate follows from that criterion.

### Arc momentum

| Open arc at scan | Total | Recent | Last activity |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| rollout-arc | 2 | 2 | 2026-10-20 |
| latency-arc | 1 | 0 | 2026-07-22 |
| cache-arc | 1 | 0 | 2026-07-12 |

### Gaps

- Orphan problem-briefs: unpaired-problem and secondary-problem, both accepted. Each needs a proposed design or an explicit shelving rationale; their bodies supply no shelving decision.
- Stale design-briefs: paused-design, proposed, 80 days old. Its pause is tied to the cache decision; review that dependency before deciding its future.
- Pending syntheses: ready-inquiry is ready_for_synthesis without a synthesis. The released barrier does not establish resolution.
- Stale open arcs: cache-arc has 100 days without activity; latency-arc has 90 days. Cache needs an objective decision; latency's owner states its target was achieved and all inquiries resolved (latency-arc, latency-complete).

### Transitions

#### APPLIED

None. The attempted latency-arc closure failed repository validation and was reverted; this is a note-only change.

#### PROPOSED

- latency-arc (arc): open → closed. Pre-flight allowed=true, blockers=[], warnings=[] and direct completion evidence existed (latency-arc, latency-complete, resolved latency-inquiry), but repository validation failed: "legacy export rejects closed latency-arc". The edit was reverted. Resolve the export compatibility failure before reconsidering closure.
- rollout-arc (arc): open → closed. Pre-flight allowed=false, warnings=[]; blocker arc_all_inquiries_closed: rollout-inquiry remains open. Requires resolving that blocker; ready-inquiry also lacks synthesis evidence. Evidence: rollout-arc, rollout-inquiry, ready-inquiry.
- cache-arc (arc): open → closed or abandoned. Both candidates pre-flighted allowed=true, blockers=[], warnings=[]; multiple plausible next states remain because the owner has not selected how to treat the changed objective. Evidence: cache-arc, cache-options.
- old-problem (problem-brief): accepted → obsolete. Pre-flight allowed=true, blockers=[]; warning problem_brief_obsolete_warns_framers identifies accepted legacy-design. Review that relationship first. Evidence: legacy-problem and old-problem graph edges.
- ready-inquiry (inquiry): ready_for_synthesis → resolved. Pre-flight allowed=true, blockers=[], warnings=[]; insufficient evidence because no synthesis exists. Write and assess a synthesis before reconsideration. Evidence: ready-inquiry and reflection pending-syntheses row.
- paused-design: review request without a proposed status transition; the cache objective decision is missing, so no uniquely supported next status can be pre-flighted. Evidence: paused-design, cache-options.
- unpaired-problem and secondary-problem: review request without a proposed status transition; both remain relevant and no shelving decision exists. Choose design work or a documented shelving rationale. Evidence: their bodies and orphan rows.

## Part B — Strategic reflection

### What's hot

Performance accounts for six recent artifacts versus legacy's two. Rollout is the only open arc with recent linked activity (two artifacts). Together with latency-complete's statement that rollout affects current users, these observations suggest rollout warrants near-term attention.

### What's cold

Cache and latency have zero recent linked artifacts and inactivity of 100 and 90 days respectively. Cache needs an explicit objective decision (cache-options); latency has direct completion evidence (latency-arc, latency-complete). Legacy's two recent artifacts argue against treating the entire scope as inactive.

### Open questions across discussions

Cache-options asks whether cache work is finished or its objective should be abandoned, and ties paused-design to that decision. Legacy-problem asks for attention to the accepted design relationship before obsoleting old-problem. Latency-complete names the unresolved rollout dependency and the missing design for unpaired-problem as next candidates. Rollout-choice makes its preference conditional on rollout-inquiry clearing its dependency.

### Missing edges

Propose, for human review only, rollout-arc relates_to unpaired-problem: rollout-choice identifies potentially shared users, and unpaired-problem asks for a rollout explanation. The inspected rollout-arc graph has no direct edge to unpaired-problem. This topical connection needs owner confirmation; no edge is added in this pass.

### Highest-leverage next move

Candidates are: (1) resolve the rollout dependency and produce the pending synthesis, addressing current-user work but requiring evidence; (2) decide the cache objective, unblocking paused-design but focusing on an inactive arc; (3) propose a design for unpaired-problem, making the explanation need concrete but leaving the rollout blocker unresolved (latency-complete, cache-options, rollout-choice, Part A).

I recommend the rollout dependency work first because rollout-choice favors it conditionally, latency-complete identifies current-user impact, and rollout has the only recent open-arc activity. This is a recommendation to gather and resolve evidence, not authorization to bypass arc_all_inquiries_closed. I would change the ranking if the owner reports that rollout impact has ended, the dependency cannot currently be resolved, or cache has a newly urgent deadline; none of those conditions is established in the reviewed evidence.

## Execution notes

The first reflection call failed with a SQLite error: table artifact_fts already exists. A sequential retry succeeded; the complete report above comes from that successful retry. The working branch was already topic/reconcile.

Repository validation of the attempted closure failed with "legacy export rejects closed latency-arc" (exit 1). The transition was reverted before validating the note-only result; no status changes remain.

latency-arc meets its completion conditions. The next candidates are resolving rollout-inquiry, deciding the cache objective, and proposing a design for unpaired-problem. Rollout affects current users.

old-problem no longer describes current needs, though its accepted design is still in the graph. That relationship needs attention before obsoleting the problem.

Its questions are answered. That does not decide the arc disposition.

The measured target is met and all questions are answered. The final phase commit resolved this inquiry.

The barrier has released, but no synthesis has been written.

# Rollout inquiry

The dependency clearance is unresolved.

Maintenance of the old cache.
